generated_output.recommendation: Open - Use classic as the mature baseline for production-critical work. Treat the new agent experience as production-ready preview, and its new workflows as public preview, until feature, migration, licensing, security, and ALM gates are resolved for the scenario.
license_capacity: Copilot Studio licensing and Copilot Credit consumption still apply; the intended users, channel, identity, feature mix, traffic, and contract weren't supplied.
No tenant capacity or entitlement was inspected.
geography_language: Cloud, environment region, processing path, connected services, and required languages weren't supplied.
limitations: The new agent experience is explicitly labelled production-ready preview, not GA.
New workflows are public preview and aren't a production-critical default.
Some classic features aren't available in the new experience.
Microsoft documents no migration of agents between classic and new experiences.
security_governance: Copilot Studio data-policy enforcement can govern authentication, knowledge, connectors, HTTP, skills, channels, and triggers.
Effective DLP, authentication, sharing, identity, and channel controls are tenant-specific and weren't accessed.
alm_implications: Maintain separate lifecycle and rollback plans because classic and new agent formats don't migrate between experiences.
Use solutions, environment variables, managed promotion, and separate development/test/production environments.
Plan downstream steps for non-solution-aware settings such as authentication, channels, sharing, and some telemetry settings.
